Did you know about that, that this person injured himself and was hospitalised? Because that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance. If we look at point 1 of the document, at the it end of point 1 it says that the Stolac municipality and Capljina, and the points that you are putting to the witness now refers to those municipalities. In points 8, it says that the commission insisted on the Muslim side that Dretelj be visited. We found no one there, so we went on to Ljubuski. And after point 8. So what it says about Ljubuski is after point 8, because you'll notice that in point 2 it says 42 civilians and 66 military men, and in point 9 when they're talking about Ljubuski it says 89 civilians and 96 military men. So the commission toured a number of prisons and in fact that is the report for all of this. It is not perhaps precise enough, but I think at that understanding corresponds best to the truth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a word, were your conditions of detention, according to you, good or bad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think they were very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. And the third person indicated in paragraph 12 is Ibro Kukic. Did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see him in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see his injuries?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What kind -- kind of injuries did he have?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: He had shrapnel injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know how he had got that injuries -- injury?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: That was when he was taken out to forced labour up at Drinovac or the territory between Stolac and Popovo Polje. And he was injured by a mortar grenade, mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Were the detainees taken to perform forced labour in that area on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that he was taken out every day, and one of the prisoners was taken out every day to perform forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Were you also taken there to perform forced labour?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What kind of forced labour did you perform there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: It was fortifying the front line by building some sort of protection walls, dugouts, various forms, carrying sandbags up to where the dugouts were being made, carrying wooden pillars that were dug into the trenches and dugouts and then filled in with stones and sand and that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just an additional explanation. You said you took part in the forced labour, in building trenches, dugouts, and so on. When you were asked, were you a volunteer or did nobody ask your opinion and just said that you were to go and do forced labour and trench work? Did you have the opportunity of saying yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My only choice was if I hid behind somebody else until they had taken as many men as they needed. That was the only thing that I could do. So if I didn't want to go, and I didn't want to go, I tried to hide behind someone in front of me. So if they pointed a finger to anybody, that person had to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Thank you. I'm going to be very specific here. You were gathered together, as far as I was able to understand you, and the person who came to get prisoners for external work, did they say, "Any volunteers, raise your hands"? Or did the person go around pointing a finger and saying, "You, you, and you"? How did this happen? How did they go about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly they selected the people who were stronger physically for the physical labour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there was nothing you could say. You didn't have a voice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Poryvaev, you have 10 minutes, and we should round up by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I hope not the whole examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, would I like you to turn to Exhibit P 02455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said the examination-in-chief. So you should finish the entire -- the examination-in-chief by 7.00, and tomorrow it will be the turn of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I only used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have the calculations of time, please. How much time has been used? Yes. You have 32 minutes, but you could proceed much faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: How did it come about that you indicated this person as an inmate who should be taken, transferred to Ljubuski once you were detained in Ljubuski? The document is dated on the 19th of May, 1993. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: On this date I was at the machine engineering faculty and not in Ljubuski. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise for interrupting, but the witness was asked whether he had seen the document, and I think I heard him say yes, that he had seen it before, but it wasn't in the transcript. But I would like to know how he saw the document, where he saw the document, and linked to the identification of the document it has neither a stamp nor a signature, and the letterhead is different than is customary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did see it. I saw this document yesterday during the preparation for the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poryvaev, you're asking him about a document dated the 19th of May, 1993, and he says he wasn't in Ljubuski. Is there any need to proceed with your questions about the document in view of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is a sense -- some sense of proceeding with this document, because I asked him where was he once he was returned to Ljubuski from someplace, and he started answering this question. He was at the mechanical faculty. And my first question was how did it come about that he was taken to the mechanical faculty and what happened to him at the mechanical faculty. That's -- it's not a futile question, I think -- I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead then. Ask him the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: You just told the Trial Chamber that you were at the mechanical faculty. Who took you there, when?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th, we had this one bathing in Capljina that I mentioned. After we returned from Capljina, there was lunch in Ljubuski. So we went from Ljubuski to Capljina with buses taking us to the former JNA barracks. We were able to wash there and go back to Ljubuski. After that we had lunch, and after lunch somebody asked whether there was a driver among us. I kept quiet, but one of the detainees said that I was a professional driver. They told that -- they told Prlic that, and Prlic called me into his office. Fejzo Plavsic and Ibro Junuzovic he took us into his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: First of all --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Don't hurry. And then you just said some Prlic. Please give the first name of that person.

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Ante Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You may go on.

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: So Ante Prlic told us to go to his office, the three of us. He talked to us and said that he needed three drivers for some job. He didn't explain what those jobs were, and he said the people would be waiting for us in front of the prison gates. He escorted us to the gates. We got into a Volkswagen van, and in the van were two policemen, two military policemen. One was doing the driving, and the other was in the van with us, and he was our escort. He escorted us with a weapon. He had his automatic rifle pointed at us so that he was sure we would be quiet. And we set off from Ljubuski. I didn't know where we were going straight away. Nobody told us anything. And when we reached Citluk, it was clear to me -- or, at Medjugorje -- I apologise for saying Citluk. It was Medjugorje. I got it wrong. We reached Medjugorje, and it was clear what terrain we were on, and we realised that we were moving towards Mostar. So we went Medjugorje, Krusevo, and descended into Mostar. That's the route we took. As we were going down to Mostar from Kuglovaca on the western side of Mostar there was -- we halted for a few minutes were able to continue on our way in a few minutes' time and went down to Mostar, and a facility that I knew which used to be the commercial bank of Sarajevo, because a long time ago I went there with my father who had a saving -- some savings in that bank, and we passed the Partisan cemetery. We waited there outside for some 10 minutes, and when we entered into Mostar, we that there was heavy fighting going on and a lot of shooting. So after 10 minutes we entered this building of the commercial bank, the commercial bank building, and when I went inside I saw the face of this man Ivan who interrogated me in Sovici and who, when he saw us at first glance, welcomed us nicely, offered us some cigarettes, and told us to sit down. And then some explanation followed. He said he needed one driver, not three drivers, but he said he called all of us three for him to choose the best. So he told three of us to come so that he could choose the best for the job he had in mind. Now, what that job was we didn't know. And then he went on to explain what the job was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, since we have too little time left, I just would like to speed up the procedure now and just start -- recount your story from the moment you were taken to the MUP station, to the mechanical faculty.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for interrupting, Your Honours. I intervene on very rare occasions, but I don't understand anything any more. If this statement was tendered according to 92 ter, the witness is going through it all again, and the Prosecutor is asking him questions on certain portions of that statement. I really don't want to interrupt the Prosecutor and that should not be done, but this is word-for-word recounting what we already have in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is exactly the observation that I was making. So what is the object of that, Mr. Poryvaev? If it's all in the written statement, why go into it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I just want to show the witness some exhibits now once he came -- we came to the mechanical faculty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And which exhibit did you wish to show him?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit P 09791.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you find this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: 09791, yes. I have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the building that is depicted on this photo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: It's the machine engineering faculty where I was detained on that day, the 17th. On the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Shortly, what happened to you at the mechanical faculty?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, what happened there was that I experienced the worst three days -- or, rather, three days and two nights of my life. And I'm almost 50 years old now. Those were the worst three days in the 10 and a half months of the time I spent in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: I was beaten up. I was beaten so badly I couldn't move. My ribs were broken and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: The military police and anybody else who had the chance to get a go. It was not only once, several times a day and several times a night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: In what part of the building were you beaten up?

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: In the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Before this, I would like the witness just to put with a pointer, make a mark on the Exhibit 09791. Put number 1 at the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: Number 1. Shall I write it down? I don't quite understand what I'm supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, mark the second one. Mark the second one, put number 1 just to identify the building.

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: On the screen you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: You may do that. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ISMET POLJAREVIC
utterances.text: You mean on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: And put your initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Poryvaev, I'm sorry. I do not understand this. We have this document in our file. It is shown to the witness. He recognises. That is in the transcript. What else do we need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Would I like this document to be captured and given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, just introduce it as a piece of evidence. Other piece are not signed by the witness. He doesn't sign all the other documents. Why should he sign this picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Because it's a photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, give us, please, an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number IC 170, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 7.00 p.m. We will continue tomorrow. How many more minutes do you immediate, Mr. Poryvaev, to finish tomorrow, because you have already used, I think, more than 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I will use all the remaining time. If I have 20 minutes, I will use 20 minutes. If I have 21 minutes, I will use 21 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
